name: New Hollywood
summary: A director's cinema inside the studios: location shooting, long lenses, a zoom, a wide anamorphic frame and flawed heroes. A story that ends without a lesson. The style looks lived in and tough.

philosophy.core_thesis: The studio picture is used for a director's personal, sceptical view, so the heroes are flawed, the places are real and the endings stay open.
design_principles: Shoot on real streets, roads and rooms, with practical lamps in the frame, and let the light fall off to dark in the corners.
Frame in 2.35:1 anamorphic or 1.85:1 and use a long lens of 85mm to 200mm to compress a street into a flat, crowded plane.
Use a slow zoom of 2 to 5 s into or out of a face, and a handheld follow of 1 to 1.5 m/s at a key moment.
Cut at an average shot length of 5 to 8 s and let a dialogue scene run in a single take of 30 to 90 s.
Print with a low-key grade, a lifted contrast of +20% and a desaturated palette of earth and brown.
Use source music from a car radio or a jukebox as the score, at −18 to −20 dB under the dialogue.
End on a freeze, an unresolved image or a bleak close, with no moral summing up.
anti_patterns: A studio back lot with a painted sky
A glamour key with a soft filter on the star
An orchestral score that tells the viewer what to feel
Back projection in a car scene
A hero with no moral flaw

composition.framing: A wide 2.35:1 frame in which the character sits small in a compressed, crowded street or a long, empty road.
composition.staging_in_depth: A long-lens stack of 3 to 5 planes, compressed; practical lamps and signs fill the back, and a foreground edge cuts into the frame.
composition.subject_placement: Off centre by 20% to 30%, with the car, the door or the window as a frame inside the frame.

principles.rule: Frame in a wide anamorphic ratio and use the door, the window or the car as a second frame inside it.
Use a long lens to stack the planes of a street into a crowded, compressed picture.
Leave the road, the desert or the dark room as a large empty mass beside the figure.
Let the practical lamps be the brightest points and let the rest fall to a low key.
principles.value: key to fill 4:1, lamps at +3 stops over the room

principles.rule: Put the character on a third line and leave the other two thirds to the place.
principles.value: figure at 25% to 33% from the edge

camera_and_movement.movement: A zoom, a handheld follow in the street and a locked-off wide for a long dialogue. Moves are motivated and a little rough.
camera_and_movement.support: Handheld Panaflex or Arriflex, a dolly and a car mount
camera_and_movement.camera_height: 1.3 to 1.7 m, eye level; a low angle from a car seat at 0.8 m
camera_and_movement.move_speed: Handheld follow 1.0 to 1.5 m/s; a zoom over 2 to 5 s

lens_and_format.focal_length: 40mm to 200mm (35mm format); a zoom of 25mm to 250mm
lens_and_format.aperture: f/2 to f/4 in low light; f/5.6 outdoors
lens_and_format.resolution: 35mm negative, grain and halation; scan at 2K or 4K
lens_and_format.focus: Selective focus on the character; a rack focus from a foreground to a face over 1 to 2 s.

light.quality: Low, practical and often underexposed, with sodium and tungsten lamps; the shadows are black and the highlights burn.
light.direction: From a window or a lamp in the frame; a bounce from the ceiling for the face.
light.colour_temperature: Tungsten 3200K lamps with daylight 5600K windows, left uncorrected
light.source: Practical lamps, windows and a bounced photoflood

colour_and_grade.treatment: A desaturated palette of brown, olive and ochre, with deep blacks and a grainy, warm print.
grade_recipe: Set the black point at 3% and let the shadows crush below 8%.
Desaturate to 70% of the original and push the midtones to warm brown by +8%.
Add a contrast curve of +20% and let the practical lamps burn to white.
Add grain at 15% to 20% and a halation of 3% around the lamps.
Do not add a teal cast; keep a single warm and earthy grade.
colour_and_grade.texture: Heavy grain at 15% to 20%, with halation around highlights

editing_and_rhythm.average_shot_length: 5 to 8 s (estimate; check Cinemetrics for each title)
editing_and_rhythm.shot_length_range: 1 s for a shock cut to 90 s for a long dialogue take
editing_and_rhythm.cutting_logic: Cut on the rhythm of the talk, and let a scene run past its point. Cut to a hard shock at the break of violence, and cut away to the road.
editing_and_rhythm.transitions: Hard cut, a freeze frame of 2 to 4 s at the close, a dissolve of 1 to 2 s, and a smash cut to black.

sound.approach: Location sound with room tone, traffic and a car radio; a layered track in which voices overlap.
sound.dialogue: Naturalistic, overlapping, with a street idiom, and a mumble that the mix does not fix.
sound.music: Source music from a jukebox, a radio or a rock record; a score that is spare, with a solo guitar or a synthesizer.
sound.loudness: −23 LUFS integrated for a restoration, with dialogue peaks at −6 dBFS

titles_and_graphics.treatment: A plain title card over a location shot or black, with a pop song; credits in a plain list.
titles_and_graphics.type: A bold sans-serif or a grotesque in white upper case, 2 to 4 s for the title and 1 to 2 s for a credit.

shot_primer.opening: Open on a location in motion, such as a road, a city street or a car, with source music; hold the first shot for 5 to 8 s.

positive: source music from a car radio

emotion.target_response: Unease and recognition: the viewer is in a real, rough place with a person who might not win.

use_cases: video prompts for a car and street scene
avoid_when: The brief needs a bright, clean, optimistic product look.
The piece must be a short vertical clip with a fast hook.

modifiers.how: Keep the 35mm and the story; use a three-point light at 3:1, a smooth dolly and a score under the scene.
Keep the anamorphic frame; add slow motion at 60 to 120 fps for the violence and cut at 2 to 3 s.

sources.title: Peter Biskind, Easy Riders, Raging Bulls (Simon & Schuster, 1998)
David Cook, Lost Illusions: American Cinema in the Shadow of Watergate and Vietnam, 1970–1979 (University of California Press, 2000)
